title: Calms down when spoken to or picked up
description: Settles, even briefly, when you talk softly, hold them close or pick them up.
activities: Hold your baby skin to skin and talk or sing quietly.
Respond to crying promptly: you cannot spoil a young baby with comfort.

title: Looks at your face
description: Studies faces during feeds and cuddles; faces are the most interesting thing they can see.
activities: Hold your face about 20–30 cm away, the distance young babies see best, and make slow expressions.

title: Seems happy to see you when you walk up
description: Brightens, quietens or moves arms and legs when a familiar carer comes close.
activities: Greet your baby by name each time you come to them.

title: Smiles when you talk to or smile at them
description: The first social smiles, in reply to your face and voice, usually appear between 6 and 8 weeks.
activities: Smile and wait: give your baby time to smile back, then respond with delight.

title: Makes sounds other than crying
description: Small gurgles, grunts and early 'ah' sounds, often when content.
activities: Copy your baby's sounds back to them, then pause so they can 'answer'.

title: Reacts to loud sounds
description: Startles, blinks, stops moving or cries at a sudden loud noise.
activities: Notice how your baby reacts to everyday sounds such as a door closing.
concern_note: If your baby never reacts to loud sounds, mention it to your health visitor or GP soon; a hearing check can be arranged at any age.

title: Watches you as you move
description: Follows a person moving nearby with their eyes, at least for a moment.
activities: Move slowly from side to side while your baby watches your face.

title: Looks at a toy for several seconds
description: Fixes their gaze on a high-contrast toy or picture for a few seconds.
activities: Show black-and-white or bold-pattern pictures during wakeful, calm times.

title: Holds head up when on tummy
description: Lifts the head briefly during tummy time.
activities: Do short spells of tummy time while awake and watched, building up to at least 30 minutes spread across the day.
Lie your baby on your chest, face to face, as a gentle start.

title: Moves both arms and both legs
description: Kicks and waves both arms and both legs, roughly equally on each side.
activities: Give unrestricted floor time on a mat so your baby can kick freely.
concern_note: If one side of the body moves much less than the other, mention it to your GP or health visitor soon.

title: Opens hands briefly
description: Hands are often fisted at first but open for short moments.
activities: Stroke the back of your baby's hand gently; it often makes the fingers open.

title: Smiles on their own to get your attention
description: Starts a smile themselves to draw you in, not only smiling back.
activities: When your baby smiles at you, respond: talk, smile and copy their expression.

title: Chuckles when you try to make them laugh
description: A chuckle or giggle that is not yet a full laugh.
activities: Try gentle surprises: funny faces, raspberries on the tummy, silly sounds.

title: Looks at you, moves or makes sounds to get or keep your attention
description: Uses eye contact, wriggling or noises to keep an interaction going.
activities: Take turns: when your baby makes a sound or moves, answer, then pause and wait for their turn.

title: Makes cooing sounds like 'oooo' and 'aahh'
description: Long vowel sounds, often in reply to your voice.
activities: Talk through what you are doing during nappy changes and feeds, leaving gaps for your baby to coo back.

title: Makes sounds back when you talk
description: Answers your talk with sounds of their own: the start of conversation.
activities: Have 'conversations': say something, wait, and reply to whatever sound your baby makes.

title: Turns head towards the sound of your voice
description: Looks round when they hear a familiar voice out of sight.
activities: Call softly from one side, then the other, and smile when your baby finds you.
concern_note: If your baby does not turn towards voices or sounds, ask your health visitor or GP about a hearing check.

title: Opens mouth when they see breast or bottle, if hungry
description: Recognises the breast or bottle and gets ready to feed.
activities: Watch for early feeding cues such as rooting and hand-to-mouth before crying starts.

title: Looks at their hands with interest
description: Discovers their own hands and watches them move.
activities: Let your baby play on their back with hands free, and offer a soft wrist rattle.

title: Holds head steady without support when you hold them
description: Head stays steady when held upright, without you supporting it.
activities: Carry your baby upright facing you or the world for short spells so they practise head control.

title: Holds a toy when you put it in their hand
description: Grips a rattle or ring placed in their hand.
activities: Offer light toys that are easy to grip, such as rings and rattles.

title: Uses an arm to swing at toys
description: Bats at toys hanging above or beside them.
activities: Hang a toy within reach on a play gym and let your baby bat at it.

title: Brings hands to mouth
description: Sucks fingers or fist, a way of exploring and self-soothing.
activities: Let your baby explore their hands; keep nails short.

title: Pushes up onto elbows or forearms when on tummy
description: Lifts head and chest on forearms during tummy time.
activities: Put a toy or a mirror in front of your baby during tummy time to encourage looking up.

title: Knows familiar people
description: Reacts differently to familiar carers than to strangers.
activities: Name the people your baby sees: 'Here's Grandma!'

title: Likes to look at themselves in a mirror
description: Smiles at, pats or 'talks' to their reflection.
activities: Use an unbreakable baby mirror at tummy time and point out 'There's you!'

title: Laughs
description: A proper belly laugh.
activities: Play simple anticipation games such as 'round and round the garden'.

title: Takes turns making sounds with you
description: Makes a sound, waits for yours, then answers: early back-and-forth.
activities: Copy your baby's sounds and wait; the pause matters as much as the talking.

title: Blows raspberries
description: Sticks the tongue out and blows.
activities: Blow raspberries back; playful mouth sounds build the muscles used for speech.

title: Makes squealing noises
description: High-pitched squeals, often when excited.
activities: Join in with the excitement and name the feeling: 'You're so happy!'

title: Puts things in their mouth to explore them
description: Uses the mouth to learn about shape and texture.
activities: Offer safe, clean toys of different textures.
safety_note: Keep small objects, coins, magnets and button batteries out of reach: anything that fits through a toilet-roll tube is a choking risk.

title: Reaches to grab a toy they want
description: Stretches out to take a toy within reach.
activities: Place toys just within reach during floor play so your baby has a reason to stretch.
safety_note: Keep hot drinks well out of reach now your baby grabs at things.

title: Closes lips to show they don't want more food
description: Turns away or keeps lips shut when they have had enough.
activities: Follow your baby's signals of fullness rather than encouraging a few more spoonfuls.

title: Rolls from tummy to back
description: Rolls over from front to back on their own.
activities: Give plenty of floor time; encourage rolling by placing a toy just out of reach to the side.
safety_note: Never leave your baby on a bed, sofa or changing table: rolling can start without warning. Still put them to sleep on their back; once they roll over themselves, you don't need to turn them back.

title: Pushes up with straight arms when on tummy
description: Lifts the chest right off the floor on straight arms.
activities: Keep up daily tummy time with toys to look at and reach for.

title: Leans on hands to support themselves when sitting
description: Sits propped forward on their hands (tripod sitting).
activities: Sit your baby on the floor between your legs or with cushions around for support.

title: Is shy, clingy or fearful around strangers
description: Wary of unfamiliar people, a sign of a strong bond with you.
activities: Let your baby watch a new person from your lap before being handed over.

title: Shows several facial expressions, like happy, sad, angry and surprised
description: Expresses a range of feelings on their face.
activities: Name feelings as they happen: 'You're cross because the ball rolled away.'

title: Looks when you call their name
description: Turns or looks up when they hear their name.
activities: Use your baby's name often, then reward the look with a smile.
concern_note: If your baby rarely responds to their name, mention it at your next health visitor contact; a hearing check is often the first step.

title: Reacts when you leave (looks, reaches for you or cries)
description: Notices and protests when a main carer goes, a normal stage of attachment.
activities: Say goodbye briefly and cheerfully rather than slipping away; come back when you said you would.

title: Smiles or laughs when you play peekaboo
description: Enjoys hiding games and anticipates you reappearing.
activities: Play peekaboo with your hands, a muslin or from behind furniture.

title: Makes lots of different sounds like 'mamamama' and 'babababa'
description: Repeated consonant–vowel babble.
activities: Babble back and add real words: 'ba-ba… ball!'
concern_note: If your baby is not babbling by around 10 months, talk to your health visitor; they may suggest a hearing check.

title: Lifts arms up to be picked up
description: Uses a gesture to ask for something: early communication without words.
activities: Respond to gestures and put words to them: 'Up? You want up!'

title: Looks for objects when dropped out of sight
description: Watches where a spoon or toy falls, understanding that things still exist when out of view.
activities: Play dropping games from the high chair and look together: 'Where did it go?'

title: Bangs two things together
description: Bangs blocks or a spoon on a pan to make a noise.
activities: Give pots, wooden spoons and blocks for banging and copy the rhythm.

title: Gets to a sitting position by themselves
description: Moves from lying to sitting without help.
activities: Give lots of time on the floor rather than in seats and walkers.

title: Moves things from one hand to the other
description: Passes a toy between hands.
activities: Offer a toy to the hand that's already holding one and see what your baby does.

title: Uses fingers to 'rake' food towards themselves
description: Pulls small foods closer with a raking sweep of the fingers.
activities: Offer soft finger foods once weaning is under way, always with your baby sitting up and watched.
safety_note: Cut small round foods such as grapes and cherry tomatoes lengthways into quarters, and always stay with your baby while they eat.

title: Sits without support
description: Sits steadily on the floor without hands or cushions.
activities: Sit your baby on the floor with toys around them to reach and turn for.

typical_window.label: Healthy children in the WHO study sat alone at anywhere from 3.8 to 9.2 months.

title: Crawls on hands and knees
description: Moves forward on hands and knees. Some babies bottom-shuffle, roll or go straight to walking instead, and that is fine.
activities: Give plenty of safe floor space and put favourite toys a little way off.
safety_note: Fit stair gates and cover sockets or move trailing cables before your baby is on the move.

typical_window.label: Babies who crawl usually start between 5.2 and 13.5 months; about 4 in 100 never crawl.

title: Plays games with you, like pat-a-cake
description: Joins in simple turn-taking games and songs with actions.
activities: Sing action rhymes such as 'pat-a-cake' and 'row, row, row your boat'.

title: Waves 'bye-bye'
description: Waves, often when prompted, to say goodbye.
activities: Wave and say 'bye-bye' every time someone leaves.

title: Calls a parent 'mama' or 'dada' or another special name
description: Uses a name for a parent on purpose.
activities: Refer to yourselves by the names you'd like your baby to use.

title: Understands 'no' (pauses or stops when you say it)
description: Briefly stops or looks at you when you say 'no'.
activities: Keep 'no' for things that matter, and say what to do instead: 'Gentle hands.'

title: Puts something in a container, like a block in a cup
description: Drops objects into a box or cup on purpose.
activities: Play 'in and out' with a tub and some blocks.

title: Looks for things they see you hide, like a toy under a blanket
description: Finds a toy hidden while they watch.
activities: Hide a toy under a cloth while your baby watches, then ask 'Where is it?'

title: Pulls up to stand
description: Uses furniture or your hands to pull up to standing.
activities: Let your baby practise barefoot on a non-slip floor.
safety_note: Lower the cot base, and fix heavy furniture such as bookcases and TVs to the wall.

typical_window.label: In the WHO study, standing with support began anywhere from 4.8 to 11.4 months.

title: Walks, holding on to furniture
description: Steps sideways along the sofa or furniture ('cruising').
activities: Arrange sturdy furniture so your baby can cruise from one piece to the next.

typical_window.label: In the WHO study, walking with support began anywhere from 5.9 to 13.7 months.

title: Drinks from a cup without a lid, as you hold it
description: Sips from an open cup you hold.
activities: Offer water in an open or free-flow cup with meals from around 6 months.

title: Picks things up between thumb and pointer finger
description: Uses a pincer grip for small bits of food.
activities: Offer small, soft pieces of food to practise picking up.
safety_note: Small objects now go straight to the mouth: keep button batteries, magnets and loose change out of reach.

title: Copies other children while playing
description: Watches other children and copies what they do, like taking toys out of a box.
activities: Go to baby groups, the park or the library so your child can watch other children.

title: Shows you an object they like
description: Holds up or brings a toy to share their interest with you.
activities: Respond with interest and name what they show you.
concern_note: Sharing interest by showing and pointing is an important social skill; if you don't see it by 15 to 18 months, mention it to your health visitor.

title: Claps when excited
description: Claps hands to show excitement.
activities: Clap and cheer together when something fun happens.

title: Hugs a soft toy or doll
description: Shows affection to a soft toy.
activities: Include soft toys in your routines: 'Teddy's going to sleep too.'

title: Shows you affection (hugs, cuddles or kisses you)
description: Starts hugs, cuddles or kisses.
activities: Return affection warmly and name it: 'What a lovely cuddle.'

title: Tries to say one or two words besides 'mama' or 'dada'
description: Uses a word or word-like sound, such as 'ba' for ball or 'da' for dog.
activities: Repeat their word back correctly and add to it: 'Ball! A red ball.'
Read together every day; point at pictures and name them.

title: Looks at a familiar object when you name it
description: Looks towards the cup, dog or ball when you say its name.
activities: Name things your child is already looking at.

title: Follows directions given with both a gesture and words
description: Gives you a toy when you hold out your hand and say 'Give me the toy'.
activities: Pair simple requests with a gesture, then praise the response.

title: Points to ask for something or to get help
description: Points at something they want or need help with.
activities: When your child points, name what they're pointing at before you hand it over.
concern_note: If your child is not pointing by 15 to 18 months, mention it at your next health visitor contact.

title: Tries to use things the right way, like a phone, cup or book
description: Holds a toy phone to the ear or 'drinks' from a cup.
activities: Give everyday objects to explore and show how they are used.

title: Stacks at least two small objects, like blocks
description: Places one block on top of another.
activities: Build towers together and enjoy knocking them down.

title: Takes a few steps on their own
description: Walks a few steps without holding on.
activities: Let your child walk barefoot indoors; hold their hands lightly rather than lifting them.

typical_window.label: In the WHO study, walking alone began anywhere from 8.2 to 17.6 months.

title: Uses fingers to feed themselves some food
description: Picks up food and gets it to their mouth.
activities: Offer finger foods at every meal and let your child feed themselves alongside spoon-feeding.

title: Moves away from you, but looks to make sure you are close by
description: Explores, then checks back with you: using you as a safe base.
activities: Stay nearby and available at the playground so your child can explore and return.

title: Points to show you something interesting
description: Points to share an interest, such as a plane in the sky, not just to ask for something.
activities: Look where your child points and talk about it: 'Yes, a big plane!'
concern_note: Pointing to share interest is an important social skill; if you have not seen it by 18 months, talk to your health visitor or GP.

title: Puts hands out for you to wash them
description: Cooperates with simple care routines.
activities: Talk through each step of routines such as washing hands.

title: Looks at a few pages in a book with you
description: Sits with you and looks at a book for a few pages.
activities: Share books every day; let your child turn the pages and choose the book.

title: Helps you dress them by pushing an arm through a sleeve or lifting a foot
description: Joins in with getting dressed.
activities: Give your child time to help with dressing, even when it's slower.

title: Tries to say three or more words besides 'mama' or 'dada'
description: Uses at least three words, even if not said clearly.
activities: Talk about what your child is doing and wait for them to join in.
Use 'serve and return': respond to every attempt to communicate.
concern_note: If your child is not using any words by 18 months, talk to your health visitor; they can suggest support and a hearing check.

title: Follows one-step directions without gestures
description: Gives you the toy when you say 'Give it to me' without holding out your hand.
activities: Give simple, clear requests one at a time.

title: Copies you doing chores, like sweeping with a broom
description: Imitates everyday jobs around the home.
activities: Let your child 'help' with simple jobs such as wiping the table.

title: Plays with toys in a simple way, like pushing a toy car
description: Uses toys for their purpose.
activities: Offer push-along toys, cars and simple puzzles.

title: Walks without holding on to anyone or anything
description: Walks independently across a room.
activities: Take short walks outside together; WHO advises at least 3 hours a day of varied physical activity from age 1.
safety_note: Use stair gates at the top and bottom of stairs, and keep doors to roads and ponds closed.

typical_window.label: In the WHO study, walking alone began anywhere from 8.2 to 17.6 months.

concern_note: If your child is not walking by 18 months, talk to your health visitor or GP.

title: Scribbles
description: Makes marks on paper with a crayon.
activities: Offer chunky crayons and large paper, and draw alongside your child.

title: Drinks from a cup without a lid and may spill sometimes
description: Holds and drinks from an open cup, with some spills.
activities: Use an open cup at meals; NHS advice is to move off bottles from around 1 year.

title: Feeds themselves with their fingers
description: Manages most finger foods alone.
activities: Eat together as a family so your child can copy you.

title: Tries to use a spoon
description: Attempts to feed themselves with a spoon.
activities: Give your child their own spoon at meals, and accept the mess.

title: Climbs on and off a sofa or chair without help
description: Climbs up and gets down safely.
activities: Give safe climbing chances at the playground or on floor cushions.
safety_note: Climbing brings windows and shelves into reach: fit window restrictors and move furniture away from windows.

title: Notices when others are hurt or upset
description: Pauses or looks sad when someone is crying.
activities: Talk about how others might feel: 'She's sad because she fell over.'

title: Looks at your face to see how to react in a new situation
description: Checks your expression before deciding how to feel.
activities: Stay calm and encouraging when your child meets something new.

title: Points to things in a book when you ask, like 'Where is the bear?'
description: Finds named pictures in a book.
activities: Ask 'Where's the…?' questions as you read together.

title: Says at least two words together, like 'More milk'
description: Puts two words together.
activities: Expand what your child says: if they say 'milk', you say 'more milk'.
concern_note: If your child is not putting two words together by around 2 years, talk to your health visitor; it is often covered at the 2 to 2.5 year review.

title: Points to at least two body parts when you ask
description: Shows you their nose, tummy or toes when asked.
activities: Sing 'heads, shoulders, knees and toes' and play naming games at bath time.

title: Uses more gestures than just waving and pointing, like blowing a kiss or nodding
description: Uses a range of gestures to communicate.
activities: Use gestures yourself, such as nodding, shrugging and thumbs up, as you talk.

title: Holds something in one hand while using the other
description: Holds a container and takes the lid off.
activities: Give containers with easy lids to open and shut.

title: Tries to use switches, knobs or buttons on a toy
description: Experiments with how things work.
activities: Offer toys with buttons and flaps, and let your child figure them out.

title: Plays with more than one toy at the same time
description: Combines toys, like putting toy food on a toy plate.
activities: Set up simple play scenes: a tea set, teddies and blocks.

title: Kicks a ball
description: Kicks a large ball forward.
activities: Play gentle kick-about in the garden or park.

title: Runs
description: Runs, even if a little unsteadily.
activities: Give daily time to run around outside.

title: Walks (not climbs) up a few stairs, with or without help
description: Walks up steps, perhaps holding a rail or your hand.
activities: Practise on a few steps together, holding hands.
safety_note: Keep stair gates in place until your child can manage stairs reliably.

title: Eats with a spoon
description: Feeds themselves with a spoon, with some spills.
activities: Offer thicker foods such as yoghurt and porridge to practise spooning.

title: Plays next to other children and sometimes plays with them
description: Plays alongside others and begins to join in.
activities: Arrange time with other children; don't expect sharing yet.

title: Shows you what they can do by saying 'Look at me!'
description: Wants you to see what they can do.
activities: Notice and praise effort: 'You climbed all the way up!'

title: Follows simple routines when told, like tidying up when you say 'It's tidy-up time'
description: Joins in with simple routines on request.
activities: Use the same words and order for daily routines, such as a tidy-up song.

title: Says about 50 words
description: Has a vocabulary of around 50 words.
activities: Read together daily and talk about the pictures.
Limit screen time: WHO advises none before 2 and no more than an hour a day at 2 to 4 years.

title: Says two or more words together, with one action word, like 'Doggie run'
description: Combines a word with an action word.
activities: Talk about what's happening as it happens: 'The dog is running!'

title: Names things in a book when you point and ask 'What is this?'
description: Names pictures in a book.
activities: Pause on a page and let your child name what they see.

title: Says words like 'I', 'me' or 'we'
description: Uses pronouns to talk about themselves.
activities: Model them naturally in your own speech.

title: Uses things to pretend, like feeding a block to a doll as if it were food
description: Pretend play with objects standing in for others.
activities: Join in pretend play and follow your child's lead.

title: Shows simple problem-solving, like standing on a small stool to reach something
description: Works out a simple way to reach a goal.
activities: Give your child a few moments to solve small problems before you step in.
safety_note: Climbing to reach things means medicines, cleaning products and laundry pods must be locked away up high.

title: Follows two-step instructions like 'Put the toy down and close the door'
description: Remembers and carries out two steps.
activities: Give two-step requests in play: 'Get your shoes and bring them here.'

title: Shows they know at least one colour
description: Points to a red crayon when asked 'Which one is red?'
activities: Name colours in everyday talk: 'Your red cup.'

title: Uses hands to twist things, like turning door handles or unscrewing lids
description: Twists lids and handles.
activities: Give jars with easy lids and screw toys to practise.
safety_note: Child-resistant caps slow children down but don't stop them: store medicines locked away.

title: Takes some clothes off by themselves, like loose trousers or an open jacket
description: Removes simple clothing.
activities: Let your child take off coat and shoes when you get home.

title: Jumps off the ground with both feet
description: Jumps with both feet leaving the ground.
activities: Jump together: over a line on the ground or into puddles.

title: Turns book pages, one at a time, when you read
description: Turns single pages.
activities: Use board books and let your child turn the pages.

title: Calms down within 10 minutes after you leave, like at nursery drop-off
description: Settles after a short time once you have gone.
activities: Keep goodbyes short and predictable, and tell your child when you'll be back.

title: Notices other children and joins them to play
description: Joins in with other children's play.
activities: Arrange regular time with other children, such as playgroups or nursery.

title: Talks with you in conversation using at least two back-and-forth exchanges
description: Keeps a short conversation going.
activities: Ask open questions and follow your child's topic.

title: Asks 'who', 'what', 'where' or 'why' questions
description: Asks questions, like 'Where is Mummy?'
activities: Answer patiently and sometimes ask back: 'What do you think?'

title: Says what action is happening in a picture or book when asked
description: Describes actions such as 'running', 'eating' or 'playing'.
activities: Ask 'What's he doing?' as you read.

title: Says their first name when asked
description: Tells you their name.
activities: Practise names in songs and games.

title: Talks well enough for others to understand, most of the time
description: Speech is mostly clear to people outside the family.
activities: Repeat back unclear words correctly without asking your child to say them again.
concern_note: If people outside the family find your child hard to understand most of the time, talk to your health visitor or GP about a speech and language referral.

title: Draws a circle when you show them how
description: Copies a circle you draw.
activities: Draw shapes together with chunky crayons or chalk.

title: Avoids touching hot objects, like a cooker, when you warn them
description: Understands simple warnings about danger.
activities: Explain simply why something is dangerous.
safety_note: Keep pan handles turned inwards and children away from the cooker even if they understand warnings.

title: Strings items together, like large beads or pasta
description: Threads large beads onto a string.
activities: Thread pasta tubes onto a shoelace together.
safety_note: Use large beads under supervision; small beads are a choking risk.

title: Puts on some clothes by themselves, like loose trousers or a jacket
description: Dresses in simple clothing.
activities: Lay clothes out in order and let your child try.

title: Uses a fork
description: Feeds themselves with a fork.
activities: Give a child-size fork at meals.

title: Pretends to be something else during play (teacher, superhero, dog)
description: Takes on roles in pretend play.
activities: Keep a dressing-up box and join in role play.

title: Asks to go and play with children if none are around
description: Seeks out other children, e.g. 'Can I play with Alex?'
activities: Arrange play dates and visits to places with other children.

title: Comforts others who are hurt or sad, like hugging a crying friend
description: Shows empathy with actions.
activities: Praise kindness when you see it.

title: Avoids danger, like not jumping from tall heights at the playground
description: Shows some judgement about risk.
activities: Let your child take small, supervised risks so they learn their limits.

title: Likes to be a 'helper'
description: Enjoys helping with tasks.
activities: Give small jobs such as putting socks in the drawer.

title: Changes behaviour based on where they are (library, playground, place of worship)
description: Adjusts behaviour to the setting.
activities: Talk ahead of time about what happens in a new place.

title: Says sentences with four or more words
description: Speaks in longer sentences.
activities: Have back-and-forth conversations about everyday things.

title: Says some words from a song, story or nursery rhyme
description: Joins in with familiar words.
activities: Sing nursery rhymes and leave a gap for your child to fill in.

title: Talks about at least one thing that happened during their day
description: Tells you about something they did, like 'I played football.'
activities: Ask about the best part of their day at teatime or bedtime.

title: Answers simple questions like 'What is a coat for?'
description: Explains what everyday things are used for.
activities: Play 'what is it for?' with everyday objects.

title: Names a few colours of items
description: Names several colours.
activities: Play 'I spy' with colours.

title: Tells what comes next in a well-known story
description: Remembers the order of a familiar story.
activities: Pause in a favourite story and ask 'What happens next?'

title: Draws a person with three or more body parts
description: Draws a person with, say, a head, arms and legs.
activities: Draw family pictures together and talk about them.

title: Catches a large ball most of the time
description: Catches a big ball thrown gently.
activities: Play catch with a large, soft ball.

title: Serves themselves food or pours water, with adult supervision
description: Spoons food onto a plate or pours from a small jug.
activities: Let your child pour from a small jug at mealtimes.

title: Unbuttons some buttons
description: Undoes large buttons.
activities: Practise on a coat with big buttons.

title: Holds a crayon or pencil between fingers and thumb (not a fist)
description: Uses a finger grip rather than a fist.
activities: Offer short crayons, which encourage a finger grip.

title: Follows rules or takes turns when playing games with other children
description: Plays simple games with rules.
activities: Play simple board and turn-taking games together.

title: Sings, dances or acts for you
description: Performs for an audience.
activities: Be an enthusiastic audience.

title: Does simple chores at home, like matching socks or clearing the table
description: Helps with simple jobs.
activities: Give a regular small job and thank them for it.

title: Tells a story they heard or made up with at least two events
description: Tells a story with a sequence.
activities: Make up stories together, taking turns to add what happens next.

title: Answers simple questions about a book or story after you read it
description: Remembers and talks about a story.
activities: Ask about the characters after reading: 'Why was the bear sad?'

title: Keeps a conversation going with more than three back-and-forth exchanges
description: Holds a longer conversation.
activities: Talk together at mealtimes without screens.

title: Uses or recognises simple rhymes (bat–cat, ball–tall)
description: Hears and plays with rhyming words.
activities: Read rhyming books and make up silly rhymes.

title: Counts to 10
description: Says the numbers 1 to 10 in order.
activities: Count stairs, toys and steps together.

title: Names some numbers between 1 and 5 when you point to them
description: Recognises some written numbers.
activities: Point out numbers on doors, buses and clocks.

title: Uses words about time, like 'yesterday', 'tomorrow', 'morning' or 'night'
description: Talks about when things happen.
activities: Talk through the day's plan in the morning and what happened at bedtime.

title: Pays attention for 5 to 10 minutes during activities
description: Stays with an activity such as story time for 5 to 10 minutes.
activities: Choose activities your child enjoys and keep screens off in the background.

title: Writes some letters in their name
description: Copies or writes a few letters of their name.
activities: Write their name together on drawings.

title: Names some letters when you point to them
description: Recognises some letters.
activities: Point out letters on signs, especially those in their name.

title: Buttons some buttons
description: Does up large buttons.
activities: Let your child practise on their own coat.

title: Hops on one foot
description: Hops on one foot a few times.
activities: Play hopscotch or 'hop like a frog' games.
